# P03 Regulatory Gap Analysis: Cris Santos Company | Utilities | Enterprise: Electric distribution utility

**Regulation to analyze:** NERC CIP Reliability Standards, 16 U.S.C. 824o; NERC CIP-002 through CIP-015
**Why:** The most mature, mandatory, auditable cyber regime among utilities (penalties up to FPA civil penalty limits, CMEP audits). Water utilities should instead use SDWA 1433 RRA; nuclear 10 CFR 73.54; gas pipelines TSA SD 2021-02 series.

## Regulatory drivers to trace in this deliverable

| ID | Requirement | Citation |
|---|---|---|
| N22-R01 | NERC CIP Reliability Standards (CIP-002 through CIP-014; CIP-015 approved) | Federal Power Act sec. 215 (16 U.S.C. 824o); 18 CFR Part 40; NERC CIP-002-5.1a, CIP-003-9, CIP-004 to CIP-014 (current enforceable versions) |
| N22-R02 | TSA Security Directive Pipeline-2021-02G (Pipeline Cybersecurity Mitigation Actions, Contingency Planning, and Testing) | TSA SD Pipeline-2021-02G, issued under 49 U.S.C. 114 |
| N22-R03 | NRC power reactor cyber security rule | 10 CFR 73.54 |
| N22-R04 | SDWA sec. 1433 Risk & Resilience Assessment / ERP (AWIA 2018 sec. 2013) | 42 U.S.C. 300i-2 |
